title: How to hear this sermon
english: This is a listening version of the sermon, Awake, You That Sleep. Charles Wesley preached it on Sunday, 4 April 1742, before the University of Oxford. John Wesley published it. Rendered in modern English.
Awake, you that sleep, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give you light. Ephesians 5:14.

title: The three parts
english: In speaking on these words, I shall, with the help of God, do three things. First, describe the sleepers to whom they are spoken. Second, press the exhortation: Awake, you that sleep, and arise from the dead. Third, explain the promise made to those who do awake and arise. Christ shall give you light.

title: Who the sleepers are
english: And first, the sleepers spoken to here. By sleep is meant the natural state of man. It is that deep sleep of the soul into which the sin of Adam has cast all who spring from his loins. It is that supineness, that indolence, and that stupidity, that insensibility to his real condition, in which every man comes into the world, and continues until the voice of God awakes him.

title: Night and darkness
english: Now those who sleep, sleep in the night (1 Thessalonians 5:7). The state of nature is a state of utter darkness, a state in which darkness covers the earth, and gross darkness the people (Isaiah 60:2). The poor unawakened sinner, however much he may know of other things, has no knowledge of himself. In this respect he knows nothing yet as he ought to know.

He does not know that he is a fallen spirit, whose only business in the present world is to recover from his fall, to regain that image of God in which he was created. He sees no necessity for the one thing needful, even that inward universal change, that birth from above, which baptism figures. That birth is the beginning of that total renewal, that sanctification of spirit, soul, and body, without which no man shall see the Lord.

Full of all diseases as he is, he fancies himself in perfect health. Fast bound in misery and iron, he dreams that he is at liberty. He says, Peace, peace, while the devil, as a strong man armed, is in full possession of his soul. He sleeps on still, and takes his rest, though hell is moved from beneath to meet him, though the pit from which there is no return has opened its mouth to swallow him up. A fire is kindled around him, yet he does not know it. Yes, it burns him, yet he does not lay it to heart.

title: Satisfied in his sins
english: By one who sleeps, then, we are to understand, and would to God we all might understand it, a sinner satisfied in his sins, content to remain in his fallen state, to live and die without the image of God. He is ignorant both of his disease and of the only remedy for it. He never was warned, or he never regarded the warning voice of God, to flee from the wrath to come. He never yet saw that he was in danger of hell-fire, or cried out in the earnestness of his soul, What must I do to be saved?

title: The deepest sleep
english: If this sleeper is not outwardly vicious, his sleep is usually the deepest of all. He may be of the Laodicean spirit, neither cold nor hot, but a quiet, rational, inoffensive, good-natured professor of the religion of his fathers, one who only professes that religion. Or he may be zealous and orthodox, and, after the most straitest sect of our religion, live a Pharisee. That is, according to the scriptural account, one who justifies himself, one who labors to establish his own righteousness as the ground of his acceptance with God.

This is the man who, having a form of godliness, denies the power of it. Yes, and he probably reviles that power, wherever it is found, as mere extravagance and delusion. Meanwhile the wretched self-deceiver thanks God that he is not as other men are: adulterers, unjust, extortioners. No, he does no wrong to any man. He fasts twice in the week, uses all the means of grace, and is constant at church and at the sacrament. Yes, and he gives tithes of all that he has, and does all the good that he can.

As to the righteousness of the law, he is blameless. He lacks nothing of godliness but the power. He lacks nothing of religion but the spirit. He lacks nothing of Christianity but the truth and the life.

title: Clean outside, dead within
english: But do you not know that, however highly esteemed among men such a Christian as this may be, he is an abomination in the sight of God, and an heir of every woe which the Son of God, yesterday, today, and forever, denounces against scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites? He has made clean the outside of the cup and the platter, but within he is full of all filthiness. An evil disease still clings to him, so that his inward parts are very wickedness.

Our Lord fitly compares him to a painted sepulcher, which appears beautiful outside, but nevertheless is full of dead men's bones, and of all uncleanness. The bones indeed are no longer dry. The sinews and flesh have come upon them, and the skin covers them above. But there is no breath in them, no Spirit of the living God.
And if any man does not have the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his. You are Christ's, if the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if not, God knows that you abide in death, even until now.

title: Dead to God
english: This is another character of the sleeper spoken to here. He abides in death, though he does not know it. He is dead to God, dead in trespasses and sins. For to be carnally minded is death. Even as it is written, by one man sin entered into the world, and death by sin, and so death passed upon all men, not only temporal death, but spiritual and eternal death as well.

In the day that you eat, said God to Adam, you shall surely die. Not bodily, unless as he then became mortal, but spiritually. You shall lose the life of your soul. You shall die to God. You shall be separated from him, your essential life and happiness.

Thus the vital union of our soul with God was first dissolved, so that in the midst of natural life we are now in spiritual death. And in this we remain until the second Adam becomes a quickening Spirit to us, a life-giving Spirit, until he raises the dead, the dead in sin, in pleasure, in riches, or in honors.

But before any dead soul can live, he hears the voice of the Son of God, and hearkens to it. He is made sensible of his lost estate, and receives the sentence of death in himself. He knows himself to be dead while he lives, dead to God and to all the things of God. He has no more power to perform the actions of a living Christian than a dead body has to perform the functions of a living man.

title: No spiritual senses
english: And it is most certain that one dead in sin does not have senses exercised to discern spiritual good and evil. Having eyes, he does not see. He has ears, and does not hear. He does not taste and see that the Lord is gracious. He has not seen God at any time, nor heard his voice, nor handled the word of life.

In vain is the name of Jesus like ointment poured out, and all his garments smell of myrrh, aloes, and cassia. The soul that sleeps in death has no perception of any objects of this kind. His heart is past feeling, and understands none of these things.

And so, having no spiritual senses, no inlets of spiritual knowledge, the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God. No, he is so far from receiving them that whatever is spiritually discerned is mere foolishness to him. He is not content to be utterly ignorant of spiritual things. He denies the very existence of them. And spiritual sensation itself is, to him, the foolishness of folly.

How, he says, can these things be? How can any man know that he is alive to God? Even as you know that your body is now alive. Faith is the life of the soul. And if you have this life abiding in you, you need no marks to prove it to yourself, except that divine conviction of the Spirit, that divine consciousness, that witness of God, which is more and greater than 10,000 human witnesses.

title: Child of the devil
english: If he does not now bear witness with your spirit that you are a child of God, O that he might convince you, you poor unawakened sinner, by his demonstration and power, that you are a child of the devil. O that, as I prophesy, there might now be a noise and a shaking, and that the bones might come together, bone to its bone. Then come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe on these slain, that they may live. And do not harden your hearts, and do not resist the Holy Ghost, who even now has come to convince you of sin, because you do not believe on the name of the only begotten Son of God.

title: God calls you now
english: Therefore, awake, you that sleep, and arise from the dead. God calls you now by my mouth, and bids you know yourself, you fallen spirit, your true state and your only concern below. What do you mean, O sleeper? Arise. Call upon your God, if perhaps your God will think upon you, so that you do not perish.

A mighty tempest is stirred up round about you, and you are sinking into the depths of perdition, the gulf of God's judgments. If you would escape them, cast yourself into them. Judge yourself, and you shall not be judged by the Lord.

Awake, awake. Stand up this moment, or you will drink at the Lord's hand the cup of his fury. Stir yourself up to lay hold on the Lord, the Lord your righteousness, mighty to save. Shake yourself from the dust. At least let the earthquake of God's threatenings shake you.
Awake, and cry out with the trembling jailer, What must I do to be saved? And never rest until you believe on the Lord Jesus, with a faith which is his gift, by the operation of his Spirit.

title: The brink of the pit
english: If I speak to any one of you more than to another, it is to you who think yourself unconcerned in this exhortation. I have a message from God to you. In his name I warn you to flee from the wrath to come. You unholy soul, see your picture in condemned Peter, lying in the dark dungeon, between the soldiers, bound with two chains, the keepers before the door keeping the prison.

The night is far spent. The morning is at hand, when you are to be brought out for execution. And in these dreadful circumstances you are fast asleep. You are fast asleep in the devil's arms, on the brink of the pit, in the jaws of everlasting destruction.

O may the angel of the Lord come upon you, and the light shine into your prison. And may you feel the stroke of an almighty hand, raising you with these words: Arise up quickly, gird yourself, and bind on your sandals, cast your garments about you, and follow me.

title: Eternity at hand
english: Awake, you everlasting spirit, out of your dream of worldly happiness. Did not God create you for himself? Then you cannot rest until you rest in him. Return, you wanderer. Fly back to your ark. This is not your home.

Do not think of building tabernacles here. You are only a stranger, a sojourner upon earth, a creature of a day, just launching out into an unchangeable state. Make haste. Eternity is at hand. Eternity depends on this moment: an eternity of happiness, or an eternity of misery.

title: Questions for the soul
english: In what state is your soul? If God, while I am yet speaking, were to require it of you, are you ready to meet death and judgment? Can you stand in his sight, who is of purer eyes than to behold iniquity? Are you fit to be a partaker of the inheritance of the saints in light? Have you fought a good fight, and kept the faith?
Have you secured the one thing needful? Have you recovered the image of God, even righteousness and true holiness? Have you put off the old man, and put on the new? Are you clothed upon with Christ?

Have you oil in your lamp? Grace in your heart? Do you love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your mind, and with all your soul, and with all your strength? Is that mind in you which was also in Christ Jesus? Are you a Christian indeed, that is, a new creature? Are old things passed away, and all things become new?

Are you a partaker of the divine nature? Do you not know that Christ is in you, unless you are reprobate? Do you know that God dwells in you, and you in God, by his Spirit which he has given you? Do you not know that your body is a temple of the Holy Ghost, which you have from God?
Have you the witness in yourself? The earnest of your inheritance? Have you received the Holy Ghost? Or do you start at the question, not knowing whether there is any Holy Ghost?

title: Have you received the Holy Ghost
english: If it offends you, be assured that you neither are a Christian, nor desire to be one. No, your very prayer is turned into sin. And you have solemnly mocked God this very day, by praying for the inspiration of his Holy Spirit, when you did not believe there was any such thing to be received.

Yet, on the authority of God's word and of our own church, I must repeat the question. Have you received the Holy Ghost? If you have not, you are not yet a Christian. For a Christian is a man who is anointed with the Holy Ghost and with power. You are not yet made a partaker of pure religion and undefiled.

Do you know what religion is? It is a participation of the divine nature, the life of God in the soul of man, Christ formed in the heart, Christ in you, the hope of glory, happiness and holiness, heaven begun upon earth. It is a kingdom of God within you (Luke 17:21), not meat and drink, no outward thing, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Ghost (Romans 14:17). It is an everlasting kingdom brought into your soul, a peace of God that passes all understanding, a joy unspeakable and full of glory.

title: Are you in earnest
english: Do you know that in Jesus Christ neither circumcision counts for anything, nor uncircumcision, but faith that works by love, but a new creation? Do you see the necessity of that inward change, that spiritual birth, that life from the dead, that holiness? And are you thoroughly convinced that without it no man shall see the Lord? Are you laboring after it? Are you giving all diligence to make your calling and election sure? Are you working out your salvation with fear and trembling, agonizing to enter in at the straight gate?
Are you in earnest about your soul? And can you tell the Searcher of hearts, You, O God, are the thing that I long for? Lord, you know all things. You know that I would love you.

You hope to be saved. But what reason do you have to give for the hope that is in you? Is it because you have done no harm? Or because you have done much good? Or because you are not like other men, but wise, or learned, or honest and morally good, esteemed by men, and of a fair reputation?
Alas, all this will never bring you to God. In his account it is lighter than vanity.

Do you know Jesus Christ, whom he has sent? Has he taught you that by grace we are saved through faith, and that not of ourselves (Ephesians 2:8)? It is the gift of God, not of works, lest any man should boast (Ephesians 2:9). Have you received the faithful saying as the whole foundation of your hope, that Jesus Christ came into the world to save sinners? Have you learned what this means: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance? I am not sent but to the lost sheep?
Are you, let the one who hears understand, lost? Dead? Damned already? Do you know your deserts? Do you feel your needs? Are you poor in spirit, mourning for God, and refusing to be comforted?

Has the prodigal come to himself, and is he well content to be thought beside himself, out of his mind, by those who are still feeding on the husks which he has left? Are you willing to live godly in Christ Jesus, and do you therefore suffer persecution? Do men say all manner of evil against you falsely, for the Son of man's sake?

title: Do not harden your hearts
english: O that in all these questions you may hear the voice that wakes the dead, and feel that hammer of the word which breaks the rocks in pieces. If you will hear his voice today, while it is called today, do not harden your hearts. Now awake, you that sleep in spiritual death, so that you do not sleep in death eternal. Feel your lost estate, and arise from the dead.

Leave your old companions in sin and death. Follow Jesus, and let the dead bury their dead. Save yourself from this untoward generation. Come out from among them, and be separate, and do not touch the unclean thing, and the Lord shall receive you. Christ shall give you light.

title: Light, grace, and glory
english: This promise I come, lastly, to explain. And how encouraging a consideration this is: whoever you are who obey his call, you cannot seek his face in vain. If even now you awake and arise from the dead, he has bound himself to give you light. The Lord shall give you grace and glory, the light of his grace here, and the light of his glory when you receive the crown that does not fade away. Your light shall break forth as the morning, and your darkness be as the noon-day. God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, shall shine in your heart, to give the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.

On those who fear the Lord shall the sun of righteousness arise, with healing in his wings. And in that day it shall be said to you, Arise, shine, for your light has come, and the glory of the Lord has risen upon you. For Christ shall reveal himself in you. And he is the true light.

God is light, and will give himself to every awakened sinner who waits for him. And you shall then be a temple of the living God, and Christ shall dwell in your heart by faith. And, being rooted and grounded in love, you shall be able to comprehend with all saints what is the breadth, and length, and depth, and height, of that love of Christ which passes knowledge.

title: The Spirit promised
english: You see your calling, brothers. We are called to be a habitation of God through his Spirit, and, through his Spirit dwelling in us, to be saints here, and partakers of the inheritance of the saints in light. So exceedingly great are the promises which are given to us, actually given to us who believe. For by faith we receive, not the spirit of the world, but the Spirit which is of God, the sum of all the promises, that we may know the things that are freely given to us of God.

The Spirit of Christ is that great gift of God, which at many times, and in various ways, he promised to man, and has fully bestowed since the time Christ was glorified. Those promises made before to the fathers he has thus fulfilled. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes. Ezekiel 36:27.
I will pour water upon him who is thirsty, and floods upon the dry ground. I will pour my Spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring. Isaiah 44:3.

title: You may know that you have received him
english: You may all be living witnesses of these things, of remission of sins, and of the gift of the Holy Ghost. If you can believe, all things are possible to him who believes. Who among you is there who fears the Lord, and yet walks on in darkness, and has no light?

I ask you, in the name of Jesus, do you believe that his arm is not shortened at all? That he is still mighty to save? That he is the same yesterday, today, and forever? That he has now power on earth to forgive sins?

Son, be of good cheer. Your sins are forgiven. God, for Christ's sake, has forgiven you. Receive this, not as the word of man, but as it is, indeed, the word of God, and you are justified freely through faith. You shall be sanctified also through faith which is in Jesus, and shall set to your seal, even yours, that God has given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.

Men and brothers, let me speak freely to you, and bear with the word of exhortation, even from one who is the least esteemed in the church. Your conscience bears you witness in the Holy Ghost that these things are so, if you have tasted that the Lord is gracious. This is eternal life, to know the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom he has sent.

This experimental knowledge, the knowledge you have tasted for yourself, and this alone, is true Christianity. He is a Christian who has received the Spirit of Christ. He is not a Christian who has not received him. Neither is it possible to have received him and not know it.

For in that day, when he comes, our Lord says, you shall know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you. John 14:20. This is that Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it does not see him, neither knows him. But you know him, for he dwells with you, and shall be in you.

title: The spirit of antichrist
english: The world cannot receive him, but utterly rejects the promise of the Father, contradicting and blaspheming. But every spirit which does not confess this is not of God. Yes, this is that spirit of antichrist, of which you have heard that it should come into the world, and even now it is in the world. He is antichrist, whoever denies the inspiration of the Holy Ghost, or denies that the indwelling Spirit of God is the common privilege of all believers, the blessing of the gospel, the unspeakable gift, the universal promise, the criterion of a real Christian.

It does not help them at all to say, We do not deny the assistance of God's Spirit, but only this inspiration, this receiving the Holy Ghost, and being sensible of it. It is only this feeling of the Spirit, this being moved by the Spirit, or filled with it, which we deny to have any place in sound religion. But in only denying this, you deny the whole Scriptures, the whole truth and promise and testimony of God.

Our own excellent church knows nothing of this devilish distinction. She speaks plainly of feeling the Spirit of Christ, of being moved by the Holy Ghost, and of knowing and feeling that there is no other name than the name of Jesus, by which we can receive life and salvation.

She teaches us all to pray for the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, yes, that we may be filled with the Holy Ghost. And every presbyter of hers professes to receive the Holy Ghost by the imposition of hands. I cite the seventeenth Article, the Office of consecrating priests, the Visitation of the sick, the Collect before the holy communion, and the Order of confirmation. Therefore to deny any of these is, in effect, to renounce the Church of England, as well as the whole Christian revelation.

title: A flood of ungodliness
english: But the wisdom of God was always foolishness with men. No wonder, then, that the great mystery of the gospel should now also be hidden from the wise and the prudent, as it was in the days of old. No wonder that it should be almost universally denied, ridiculed, and exploded, cast out as mere frenzy, and that all who still dare avow it are branded with the names of madmen and enthusiasts. This is that falling away which was to come, that general apostasy of all orders and degrees of men, which even now we find to have overspread the earth.

Run to and fro in the streets of Jerusalem, and see if you can find a man, a man who loves the Lord his God with all his heart and serves him with all his strength. How does our own land mourn, that we look no farther, under the overflowings of ungodliness? What villainies of every kind are committed day by day, yes, too often with impunity, by those who sin with a high hand, and glory in their shame? Who can reckon up the oaths, curses, profaneness, blasphemies, the lying, slandering, evil-speaking, the Sabbath-breaking, gluttony, drunkenness, revenge, the whoredoms, adulteries, and various uncleanness, the frauds, injustice, oppression, extortion, which overspread our land as a flood?

And even among those who have kept themselves pure from these grosser abominations, how much anger and pride, how much sloth and idleness, how much softness and effeminacy, how much luxury and self-indulgence, how much covetousness and ambition, how much thirst for praise, how much love of the world, how much fear of man, is to be found? Meanwhile, how little of true religion? For where is he who loves either God or his neighbor as God has given us commandment?

On the one hand are those who have not so much as the form of godliness. On the other, those who have the form only. There stands the open sepulcher, and there the painted sepulcher. So that in very deed, whoever looked earnestly at any public gathering of the people, and I fear those in our churches are not to be excepted, might easily perceive that the one part were Sadducees, and the other Pharisees. The one have almost as little concern about religion as if there were no resurrection, neither angel nor spirit. The other make it a mere lifeless form, a dull round of external performances, without either true faith, or the love of God, or joy in the Holy Ghost.

title: The salt of this place
english: Would to God I could except us of this place. Brothers, my heart's desire, and my prayer to God for you, is that you may be saved from this overflowing of ungodliness, and that here its proud waves may be stayed. But is it so indeed? God knows, yes, and our own conscience knows, it is not. You have not kept yourselves pure. Corrupt are we also, and abominable.

Few there are who understand any more. Few worship God in spirit and in truth. We too are a generation that has not set our hearts aright, and whose spirit does not cling steadfastly to God. He has appointed us indeed to be the salt of the earth. But if the salt has lost its savor, it is from then on good for nothing but to be cast out, and to be trodden under the foot of men.

title: Wrath, and a call to repent
english: And shall I not visit for these things, says the Lord? Shall not my soul be avenged on such a nation as this? Yes, we do not know how soon he may say to the sword, Sword, go through this land. He has given us a long space to repent. He lets us alone this year also. But he warns us, and awakens us, by thunder.

His judgments are abroad in the earth. And we have every reason to expect the heaviest of all, even that he should come to us quickly and remove our candlestick out of its place, unless we repent and do the first works, unless we return to the principles of the reformation, the truth and simplicity of the gospel. Perhaps we are now resisting the last effort of divine grace to save us. Perhaps we have nearly filled up the measure of our iniquities, by rejecting the counsel of God against ourselves, and calling out his messengers.

O God, in the midst of wrath remember mercy. Be glorified in our reformation, not in our destruction. Let us hear the rod, and him who appointed it. Now that your judgments are abroad in the earth, let the inhabitants of the world learn righteousness.

My brothers, it is high time for us to awake out of sleep, before the great trumpet of the Lord is blown, and our land becomes a field of blood. O may we soon see the things that make for our peace, before they are hidden from our eyes. Turn us, O good Lord, and let your anger cease from us. O Lord, look down from heaven, behold and visit this vine, and cause us to know the time of our visitation.

Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of your name. O deliver us, and be merciful to our sins, for your name's sake. And so we will not go back from you. O let us live, and we shall call upon your name. Turn us again, O Lord God of hosts. Show the light of your countenance, and we shall be whole.

title: Glory through all ages
english: Now to him who is able to do exceeding abundantly above all that we can ask or think, according to the power that works in us, to him be glory in the church by Christ Jesus throughout all ages, world without end. Amen.
